Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Support), Lena Ortiz (DataHarbor SRE), Tom Hargreaves (Product), Priya Rao (Eng Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Customer reports intermittent 5xx spikes and timeouts during peak cadence between 09:30-10:15 local, correlated with longer sequences and burst traffic. Redwood SE suspects tokenization-induced sequence length blowup + upstream proxy rate-limit cascade; recommended adaptive backoff + raising short TTL for K-V cache prefixes. Action: Redwood to share traces & config, customer to run focused load test.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're set for about 50 minutes, quick agenda: recap incident, root cause hypotheses, mitigation we've trialed, next steps. lena, do you want to start with impact?
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: yeah thanks Maya, um so we've been seeing these intermittent 5xxs, it's not constant, it's primarily during our morning ingest window, we saw about 2.1% error rate spike for 20 minutes yesterday, timeouts too - some requests hit 30s and then fail.
[00:33] Priya Rao: and to add, product noticed downstream retries are compounding, our client SDK retries at app level so we're seeing a retry storm occasionally.
[00:42] Tom Hargreaves: to be clear, this is POC, we're trying to validate expected SLA; 2% spike is a bit scary for the team but not showstopper if we have a mitigation plan.
[00:52] Diego Alvarez: okay thanks, quick background — we looked at the traces you shared, request ids 8c3f-... and 9b2a-..., and saw 5xx originating near the inference node, with "context length" jumps to 8k tokens for several requests, that leads to mem pressure.
[01:10] Lena Ortiz: 8k tokens? we thought our average was more like 800-1200, where is the 8k coming from?
[01:15] Diego Alvarez: good question. it appears tokenization mismatch—some inputs include preambles from other services, like a logging blob or full transcript pasted in, so the sequence length unexpectedly jumps. also remembered you turned on full-text embeddings enrichment, that concatenates history.
[01:29] Priya Rao: ugh, yeah that enrichment pipeline appends previous messages, we probably missed a guard there.
[01:33] Maya Chen: that explains the long tails. long sequences push the runtime into a slow path, sometimes causing an OOM or just taking too long, then our frontend gateway returns 502/504 or 500 depending on where the failure hits.
[01:47] Samir Patel: quick note — logs show a pattern where many of the 5xx responses are 500 internal with CUDA OOM-ish stack traces, others are 504 gateway timeouts when a downstream cache misses and model starts full decode.
[01:59] Lena Ortiz: interesting, can you point to whether it's model failure vs infra? we have Dedicated capacity on the roadmap but currently hosted test cluster.
[02:06] Diego Alvarez: the traces show both: model memory pressure for very long sequences (model-level), and in parallel a rate-limit cascade — when a few requests slow down, upstream retry logic floods the service, hitting API rate limit and then circuit breakers trigger.
[02:22] Tom Hargreaves: that's the retry storm Priya mentioned. so we have two interacting issues: large sequence requests and burst retries.
[02:29] Maya Chen: exactly. mitigation we recommend short term: 1) Input validation at the client to cap token length and strip enrichment payloads; 2) Implement adaptive backoff + jitter on client retries to avoid synchronized retry storms; 3) Enable shorter K-V cache TTL for session prefixes to reduce cache miss penalty until cadence stabilizes.
[02:46] Priya Rao: on the client cap, we can add a hard limit and a fallback summarization step. downside is quality might dip but better than cascading 5xxs.
[02:54] Diego Alvarez: also on Redwood side, we can try a soft-fail policy: if sequence length > threshold, route to a fall-back model variant with chunked decoding or a smaller context model, that reduces mem pressure. we can also temporarily increase per-customer concurrency queue depth if you want to test.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: do you have an automatic routing rule we can turn on for the POC?
[03:14] Diego Alvarez: yes we can add a routing policy in the console: "if tokens > 3000 then route to model-x-small or lower max_gen_tokens" — it's a quick config. we can push it as an experiment for 24-48h.
[03:24] Tom Hargreaves: what about rate limits? we already bumped the app-level client retry count to 3 — maybe that's too aggressive.
[03:30] Maya Chen: right, the interaction is key. recommend adaptive backoff: base backoff 200ms with exponential and jitter, cap retries to 2 for high-cost endpoints. Diego can share a sample backoff config.
[03:42] Samir Patel: we also toggled a gateway timeout default from 30s to 45s for a short window which reduced 504s but increased queueing, so it traded off latency for fewer client-level timeouts. not sustainable.
[03:55] Lena Ortiz: was the 5xx correlated with certain model versions or quantization formats? we saw two model variants in the deployment.
[04:03] Diego Alvarez: good catch — the 8-bit quantized variant had slightly different memory behavior; some requests with longer contexts worked fine on the float16 variant but cost more. we saw ~10% higher OOMs on 8-bit in the traces.
[04:18] Priya Rao: might be worth temporarily pinning to float16 for heavy windows while we tune. cost tradeoff acknowledged.
[04:24] Maya Chen: agreed. short-term options summary: client-side token cap + summarization; enable routing-to-small-model for huge inputs; temporary float16 pin during peak; adaptive backoff + reduce retry count; and Redwood will supply annotated traces + a config bundle for testing.
[04:41] Tom Hargreaves: ok what's the plan to reproduce? lena, can you run a synthetic burst with the script you used earlier?
[04:47] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll run a 30-minute ramp test tomorrow morning, pushing to 1.5x normal peak, with a mix of long and normal requests. we'll tag traces and send to Redwood.
[04:56] Diego Alvarez: perfect — please include request ids and full request payloads (strip PII) and we'll correlate. we'll also instrument an additional metric for "sequence length distribution" so we can alert earlier.
[05:08] Priya Rao: what about permanent solutions — is Dedicated going to fix this?
[05:12] Maya Chen: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor and gives predictable throughput, but it doesn't eliminate pathological long-context OOMs. Dedicated + routing + model pinning gives the highest reliability in production. For regulated teams, Private deploy is an option too.
[05:24] Lena Ortiz: any SOC2 / security concerns with sharing traces? some traces include user identifiers.
[05:29] Samir Patel: please strip PII before upload; we accept encrypted archives, and we can support S3 presigned links or your secure share. Redwood is SOC2 compliant for hosted PII handling, but for the POC we recommend masked traces.
[05:41] Tom Hargreaves: we also have an internal proxy that adds headers; sometimes headers include base64 blob of full message - that's likely the enrichment payload causing the long context.
[05:51] Diego Alvarez: noted. action item: add request-side max-token guard + sample summarizer in SDK we can ship as a patch. we already have a small JS snippet for that.
[06:00] Maya Chen: i'll share the snippet and the backoff policy samples after the call.
[06:04] Lena Ortiz: on monitoring, can Redwood emit a per-customer sequence length percentile metric into our console so we can alert at 95th > 2k tokens?
[06:12] Diego Alvarez: yes we can create a per-tenant telemetry chart; we will add a 95th/99th token length gauge and a 5xx rate alert.
[06:21] Priya Rao: timeline and owners?
[06:24] Maya Chen: quick recap and owners — Diego will collect and annotate the 5xx traces and push an experiment routing rule by 2026-03-30; Maya will send pricing + Dedicated options by 2026-03-29; Lena will run the synthetic test and upload results by 2026-04-02; Diego will push adaptive backoff config sample by 2026-03-31.
[06:40] Tom Hargreaves: ok makes sense. any blockers on Redwood side for routing experiment?
[06:45] Diego Alvarez: none, it's console config; we'll enable feature-flagged rule on a fraction of traffic (10%) first.
[06:50] Samir Patel: quick note regarding logs: we may need the full agent logs from your proxy to see header size growth, not just the payload. Lena, can you grab those as well?
[07:00] Lena Ortiz: yes, we'll include proxy logs where available.
[07:04] Priya Rao: curious — did we consider changing client SDK retry behavior instead of server side? we can push change faster on our side.
[07:10] Maya Chen: ideal is both: client reduces retry aggressiveness to prevent storms, server adds routing/fallback as defense-in-depth.
[07:16] Diego Alvarez: one more data point — we noticed a small period where a downstream cache missed because of prefix variance, that increased token generation. an option is to normalize session keys so K-V cache hits improve.
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: will check enrichment pipeline to ensure consistent session keys.
[07:33] Tom Hargreaves: any implications for evals / quality? if we summarise inputs preemptively, some cases could degrade. we'll need to measure quality delta.
[07:40] Diego Alvarez: totally — recommend A/B on a small fraction for quality guardrails, Redwood Optimize can run a quick eval on a representative prompt set.
[07:48] Maya Chen: ok last minute items — competitors question: we discussed other providers; nothing materially different for long-context handling right now, most vendors will hit similar memory limits unless they shard or use specialized long-context kernels.
[08:00] Priya Rao: noted. thanks everyone.
[08:04] Maya Chen: we'll follow up with the bundle: 1) annotated traces, 2) backoff snippet, 3) routing rule to try, 4) sample load script. next call: let's do a short sync after Lena runs the test, propose 2026-04-03.
